title: Tenant Onboarding: Acceptance Testing & Telemetry Assertions
author: Aisha Kaur
summary: A structured acceptance-testing playbook to validate tenant readiness after provisioning and before hand-back. Defines telemetry assertions, synthetic scenarios, and safe rollback/fallback steps tailored to Dedicated and Private tenants.
body:
Purpose

This playbook provides a repeatable acceptance-testing and telemetry-assertion checklist for enterprise tenant cutovers (Dedicated and Private modes). Its goal is to ensure customers meet their SLOs and observability expectations before the CX hand-off.

Scope and audience

- Audience: Customer Success Engineers (CSE), Solutions Engineers, Oncall SREs, and Platform Engineers executing go-live validation.
- Scope: Post-provisioning validation window (first 72 hours), focused on latency, error rates, throughput, billing signals, and data-plane connectivity. Not intended for long-term performance tuning.

Prerequisites

1. Tenant is provisioned and accessible; operator has admin token and tenant ID.
2. Telemetry forwarding (metrics/traces/logs) enabled to central telemetry workspace or customer-managed forwarder.
3. Canary API key created and injected into test harness.

Quick checklist (high level)

- [ ] DNS / network reachability verified (ping, curl).
- [ ] TLS certificate chain validated for private endpoints.
- [ ] Basic API call succeeds and returns expected schema.
- [ ] Ingress egress firewall rules allow control-plane callbacks (if Private).
- [ ] Telemetry streams ingest baseline synthetic traffic.

Acceptance criteria (signal-level)

Provide these pass/fail assertions to the customer and engineering stakeholders. If any assertion fails, execute the rollback/fallback procedure below.

| Signal | Metric | Assertion (pass) |
|---|---:|---|
| Availability | 5m rolling availability | >= 99.5% during acceptance window |
| Latency (generate) | p95 gen latency | <= 600ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) |
| Error rate | 1m error rate (5xx + 429) | < 0.5% |
| Throughput | steady-state rps | Sustains expected commit profile ±10% |
| Cost signal | estimated projected daily token cost | Within agreed finance cap ±15% |
| Telemetry lag | metric ingestion lag | < 60s for critical alerts |

Telemetry assertions (concrete checks)

- Metrics to assert in the first 72 hours:
  - request.count by route and model variant
  - request.latency.p50/p95/p99 by route
  - request.errors.5xx and request.errors.ratelimit
  - kvcache.hit_ratio and kvcache.miss_ratio (if KV cache enabled)
  - pod.resource.cpu_util and pod.resource.gpu_util per node pool
  - billing.estimate.daily_tokens and billing.estimate.24h_projection

- Alert thresholds to temporarily enable for acceptance:
  - latency.p95 > 800ms for 2 consecutive 1m windows -> Sev2
  - errors.5xx >= 1% for 3 consecutive 1m windows -> Sev2
  - telemetry.lag > 120s -> Sev3

Synthetic test scenarios (run in order)

1) Smoke: Basic generation and embeddings
   - Command: curl -X POST https://{tenant-host}/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer {canary_key}" -d '{"prompt": "Hello world","max_tokens": 20}'
   - Expected: 200 OK, model output length <= 40 tokens, schema contains request_id and latency_ms

2) Latency profile: Burst of short prompts
   - Run: 100 short prompt requests over 60s (ramp 0->100rps) using our load harness
   - Expected: p95 latency within asserted bound; no tail errors or rate-limit biasing normal routes

3) Throughput profile: Sustained throughput at committed RPS
   - Run: sustained RPS for 15 minutes equal to tenant commit (or 50% of commit if in dry-run)
   - Expected: no autoscaler thrash; no OOMs on pods; stable CPU/GPU util curves

4) KV cache warm/cold cycle (if enabled)
   - Run a prefix-heavy scenario, measure kvcache.hit_ratio rising above 40% within 5 minutes for typical workloads

5) Failure injection: Simulate model fallback
   - Trigger: mark primary variant unhealthy via platform toggle; confirm automatic routing to fallback variant within policy window and acceptable quality degradation metrics tracked

Operational commands and tooling

- Test harness quickstart (example):
  - docker run --rm -e TENANT_HOST={tenant-host} -e API_KEY={canary_key} redwood/load-harness:latest --script short-burst.json

- Curl example for telemetry assertion (prometheus query):
  - curl -s "https://telemetry.redwood.internal/api/v1/query?query=request_latency_p95{tenant=\"{tenant_id}\"}" | jq .data.result

Rollback and fallback (safe steps)

If acceptance fails for any critical assertion, follow the safe rollback below in order. Document each step in the ticket.

1. Pause customer traffic (edge ACL or routing flag). Record timestamp.
2. If degraded due to model variant, revert routing to the last verified variant (platform toggle):
   - UI: Console -> Tenants -> {tenant} -> Traffic routing -> Revert to stable
   - API: POST /api/v1/tenants/{tenant}/routing?action=revert&to=stable
3. If resource saturation (OOMs/GC spikes): scale up GPU pool by +1 node or apply temporary burst capacity policy.
4. If networking (Private) issues: re-run firewall handshake and verify peering configurations; escalate to network infra.
5. If cost projection exceeded: engage FinOps and set soft quota throttle at 90% of projected cap.

Post-acceptance handback checklist

- Confirm all temporary high-sensitivity alerts are returned to normal thresholds.
- Remove canary API key and rotate if requested.
- Share a short acceptance report with: customer, AE, CSE, and Platform owner. Report should include: acceptance window metrics snapshot, synthetic script outputs, and any remediation performed.
- Schedule QBR readiness meeting within 30 days to review long-term SLOs and cost profile.

Telemetry dashboard templates (recommended panels)

- Tenant Overview: availability, p95/p99 latency, error rate, synthetic test pass/fail
- Model Variants: per-variant request count, fallbacks, average latency
- Resource Utilization: per-node GPU/CPU, pod restarts, OOM counts
- Cost: 24h token estimate, projected 7d and 30d spend

Appendix: Example acceptance report snippet

- Acceptance window: 2026-02-10 02:00 -> 2026-02-10 08:00 UTC
- p95 latency (generate, short prompts): 412ms
- Availability: 99.92%
- kvcache.hit_ratio: 46% after warm-up
- Actions performed: Increased burst capacity by 1 node at 02:45 UTC; reverted routing at 03:10 UTC after model health check.
